scope: make the audit report what it can actually prove, and say so

added.what: a rule sitting behind an `if (` whose condition contains a regex literal that matches the empty string may never run
added.howJudged: the literal is extracted and handed to the engine: new RegExp(body).test('') -- not text matching
added.whyNotTextMatching: the first version matched // inside /^https?:\/\// and flagged a healthy rule -- the same substitution of spelling for property that this audit exists to catch
added.verdict: false positive, fixed by the engine-based judgement; both kits now report zero suspects
added.commentHandling: fully commented-out add(...) no longer counts as a rule; trailing comments are kept on purpose, because a // inside a URL string is indistinguishable to a scanner this simple and dropping a live rule is worse
added.auditTests: 9 tests for the audit itself, now run by both kits' npm test -- verify-kit's glob did not reach a root test/ directory until this round

honestLimit.statement: static analysis cannot tell a dead rule from an untested one. A rule with no firing test has the same symptom either way, and only a person writing that test learns which.
honestLimit.wordingInOutput: either untested or unreachable; writing the firing test is what distinguishes them
honestLimit.evidence: all three dead rules found so far -- subject-empty, sku-empty, empty-heading -- were found by writing the test and watching it fail to fail, not by the audit diagnosing them

catalog.state: open, awaiting the batch merge queue
